No model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are null across the set), so full-model AUROC values are not directly comparable as PRS performance and are likely covariate-influenced (domain_knowledge). Within the large coherent Cancer PRSweb family (PGS000607–PGS000616), the GWAS-hits / P+T / lassosum siblings share essentially identical endpoint and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), making their reported full-model AUROC more comparable; among them, PGS000611 shows the strongest available risk-stratification signal (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.66, 95% CI 1.79–3.93) with similar per-SD OR (~1.284) and AUROC (~0.567) to close siblings, and uses a simple 13-variant GWAS-hits construction consistent with bladder cancer’s potentially oligogenic architecture noted in the domain guidance. Main limitation: selection is constrained by missing PRS-only metrics and heterogeneous reporting across publications (e.g., very high full-model AUROC in PGS000071/PGS000782 likely reflects added epidemiologic covariates), so the evidence does not support a single unequivocal best model.

final_decision.rationale: Visible records support the picker’s choice. Most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R², so the very high full-model AUROC values in PGS000071/PGS000782 (~0.80) are not comparable as standalone PRS performance and are plausibly driven by their extensive covariate set (age/sex/PCs plus smoking variables and BMI). In contrast, the Cancer PRSweb cluster (PGS000607–PGS000616) is internally comparable: same endpoint family (“Cancer of bladder”), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), and similar evaluation setting. Within that cluster, PGS000611 (GWAS hits, 13 variants; UKB dev; EUR eval) has one of the strongest and cleanest risk-stratification signals reported (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.66, CI 1.79–3.93) while maintaining similar per-SD OR (~1.28) and AUROC (~0.57) to close siblings, making it a reasonable primary among the most comparable set. Alternatives either (a) have weaker/less interpretable metrics (e.g., partial-r only in portability scores), (b) have unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS000152), or (c) shift phenotype (urothelial carcinoma) and still lack comparable discrimination metrics (PGS003335). No heritability lookup is needed because the main uncertainty is metric comparability/covariate packaging rather than plausibility of a PRS-only R² claim.

initial_decision.rationale: All five candidates are direct matches to urolithiasis or near-synonymous endpoints (urinary calculus; calculus of kidney and ureter; nephrolithiasis/ureterolithiasis). However, most models lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) and rely on limited performance reporting, making a clearly high-quality pick difficult. PGS002075 (Urinary calculus; EFO urolithiasis) is preferred because it has strong phenotype alignment (direct urolithiasis label), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (731,196), and reports a PRS-comparable performance signal (partial correlation 0.0385 with CI) in European validation. Key limitation: the available metric is partial-r rather than PRS-only AUROC/R², and competing models either provide different/non-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS001250 reports full-model AUROC and is from a pan-trait sparse framework; PGS004493/PGS004563 report only modest ORs with unknown covariates), so the evidence remains insufficient for a high-confidence, high-quality designation.

final_decision.rationale: Confirming PGS002075 as the best available choice from the visible candidates. It has the cleanest endpoint alignment to the target trait (urolithiasis via “Urinary calculus”, trait_efo=urolithiasis) and, among the two portability-paper siblings with comparable phenotype/covariates/validation context (PGS001864 vs PGS002075), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with much broader variant coverage and a slightly stronger PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0385 vs 0.0323 in EUR). The main alternative with explicit AUROC (PGS001250) is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework and its headline AUROC is largely full-model/covariate-driven (PGS-only AUROC ~0.567; small incremental AUROC), making it less compelling as a standalone PRS despite having more complete metrics. The 2024 Commun Biol models (PGS004493/PGS004563) are endpoint-close but provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) with unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, so they do not clearly surpass the LDpred2 portability score on the available evidence. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity and the relative quality/interpretability of the reported PRS-comparable metrics rather than on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS R²/AUC.

initial_decision.rationale: Direct-match candidates for type 2 diabetes mellitus are abundant and many are endpoint-aligned (e.g., multiple models with phenotyping_reported as Type 2 diabetes / incident type 2 diabetes). However, across the visible set, most reported discrimination is full-model AUROC/C-index with heterogeneous and sometimes heavy clinical covariates (e.g., fasting glucose, lipids, family history), which domain guidance flags as non-comparable to standalone PRS performance; many models also lack explicit PRS-only metrics. PGS000014 is selected as the best-supported direct-match because it is explicitly for T2D, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (6,917,436), is developed on multiple established T2D-relevant cohorts (DIAGRAM/EPIC/GERA/UKB), and provides a PRS-only R2 (0.029) alongside a European validation record, enabling at least some PRS-comparable performance grounding. Limitation: the pool contains other strong, endpoint-faithful candidates (including newer and/or multi-ancestry and ensemble-style scores) but their PRS-only metrics are often missing or not directly comparable, preventing a clearly high-confidence single winner from the provided metadata alone.

final_decision.rationale:
I would revise the pick away from PGS000014 because, within the visible direct-match set, there is at least one endpoint-faithful alternative that provides *cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence* while remaining methodologically strong.

- PGS000014 (LDpred; ~6.9M variants) is a reasonable disease-focused choice and does report a PRS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029. However, its headline discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.73 with covariates (age/sex/PCs/chip), and it does not provide an explicit PRS-only AUROC.
- PGS001294 (snpnet; 3,496 variants) targets non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in a time-to-event setting, which is still a close operationalization of T2D in UKB-style phenotyping. Crucially, it reports both PRS-only AUROC=0.63582 and PRS-only R2=0.03413 (plus incremental AUROC), giving a clearer, directly comparable readout of standalone PRS signal than PGS000014’s covariate-adjusted R2 alone.

Given the picker’s own concern that many candidates’ high full-model metrics are covariate-driven and non-comparable, the presence of explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 in PGS001294 is a meaningful upgrade in interpretability for selecting a primary PRS from metadata. I’m not using heritability here because the decision hinges on metric comparability/availability rather than plausibility of an extreme R2.

initial_decision.rationale: Direct-match candidates for the target concept (uterine cancer) are present, including exact/near-exact uterine endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial/uterine endometrial carcinoma (PGS000075, PGS000786, PGS002300, PGS002735-002737, PGS003381, PGS004244). Given domain guidance that endometrial carcinoma is the dominant subtype of uterine carcinoma (~90% of cases), endometrial-carcinoma endpoints are acceptable direct matches and can be preferred when better supported. Among these, PGS003381 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), uses a genome-wide method (lassosum) with large variant count (529,365), and reports a relatively strong full-model AUROC (0.761) with basic covariates (age, top 20 PCs), making it the best-supported choice from the visible metadata. However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), making cross-model comparability imperfect; additionally, an exact-label uterine cancer model exists (PGS001795) with a PRS-comparable R2 reported (Nagelkerke’s R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.001948) but it comes from a global biobank framework context and shows modest discrimination evidence, leaving some unresolved tradeoff between exact-label/PRS-comparable metric availability vs stronger structural properties and endpoint-dominant-subtype alignment.

final_decision.rationale: Visible candidates include both exact/umbrella uterine cancer endpoints (e.g., PGS000541/PGS000542/PGS001795) and endometrial-carcinoma endpoints (dominant uterine subtype) including PGS003381. On the metadata shown, PGS003381 has the strongest overall evidence package for the target concept: high endpoint fidelity to a uterine cancer diagnosis subtype (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), a genome-wide construction with substantial variant coverage (lassosum; 529,365 variants), and evaluation with relatively clean/basic covariates (age + genetic PCs). The main alternatives either (a) are small GWAS-hits/P+T uterine scores with clearly weaker discrimination (PGS000541/PGS000542 full-model AUROC ~0.57), or (b) are framework-style global-biobank PRS (PGS001795) that does provide a PRS-comparable R2 but it is very small and the study archetype is less disease-focused, making it a weaker replacement despite the metric type advantage. Several endometrial scores report higher full-model AUROC (~0.75) but are based on very small SNP sets and/or include heavier covariate packaging (e.g., family history, BMI, reproductive factors), so their AUROC is less attributable to the PRS itself than PGS003381’s cleaner setup. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision is driven by endpoint fidelity + method/variant coverage + covariate cleanliness, and no candidate presents a PRS-only R2/AUC close to a plausible h2 ceiling that would create a concrete sanity-check conflict.
